feedback: Decision: approve. This candidate is the baseline from entityR2A (score 124.80) with one targeted change: kp 3.0 to 3.5, with kd 0.30, the widened spread (x = ±0.024 m), the 0.016 m footprint and base_speed 1.5 all kept. The evidence is the earlier race: line_loss_events were 1.1 on the oval, 2.0 on the s-bend and 1.0 on the slalom, and max_error stayed at about 0.061 to 0.063 m, just over the 0.06 m limit. The change is valid (sensor positions, footprint and weights are inside the contract, and line_loss is last_direction) and is a small, reasoned step from the best raced design. I have no measured result for it, so I make no claim about how it will perform. Once it races, read the results as follows. If line losses fall and max_error drops below 0.06 on some tracks, keep kp 3.5 and look at the remaining off-track cases on the s-bend. If steering_oscillation rises well above the 0.17 (oval) and 0.23 (s-bend) seen in entityR2A, lower kd to 0.20 before changing kp. If max_error is still above 0.06 with no oscillation rise, try kp 4.0 next. If the oval completes with time well under 3.0 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 to 0.2, since speed is not yet the binding limit.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.25 on the s-bend or the oval after kp 3.5, set kd to 0.20 and keep kp at 3.5, because entityR2A oscillation was 0.17 to 0.23 at kd 0.30.
If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more per run and max_error stays above 0.06, try kp 4.0 with kd 0.30, since kp 3.0 to 3.5 is the only change in this step.
If the oval completes with completion_time well under 3.0 s and progress reaches 1, raise base_speed to 1.7 in one step, with kp and kd unchanged, because the one finish in entityR2A took 1.87 s.
